content.heading: Extending the Utility of Legacy UNFCCC CDM CERs
content.subtitle: Join to know what comes next for Legacy CERs before the CDM registry closes
content.description:
The CDM stops accepting cancellations on 25 November 2026 and shuts for good on 31 December. That leaves roughly 1.275 billion legacy CERs, worth close to USD 6.4 billion, at risk unless holders act before the deadline.

Hosted by UNMAI Carbon Solutions, this session breaks down what's actually available before the deadline — from Article 6.4 transition to our Legacy CERs Platform for voluntary cancellation, reissuance, and trading.

cards.title: Current Status of Legacy CDM CERs
cards.description: The registry approaches closure on 31 December 2026 (cancellations cease on 25 Nov). Learn the direct implications for credits already issued across international accounts.

cards.title: Integrity Frameworks & Voluntary Markets
cards.description: A global perspective on how international integrity frameworks (ICVCM, VCMI) and voluntary carbon markets are positioning legacy credits as the Kyoto CDM era concludes.

cards.title: Preserve Value vs Extinction Pathways
cards.description: An assessment of available options ahead of the deadline, clarifying which transition pathways preserve credit utility and economic value versus those resulting in extinction.

cards.title: UNMAI Legacy CERs Platform Walkthrough
cards.description: A guided demonstration of UNMAI's purpose-built platform: voluntary cancellation, 1:1 digital reissuance, provenance tracking, and active institutional trading.
